about: Documents' tools for agents (through Agent Link): name, what it does, its arguments as JSON Schema, its group, whether it changes the document.

drawing_make.description: Make a dimensioned drawing of bodies in one call, and its SVG, PDF and DXF files. The drawing is an ordinary TechDraw page: template, title block, views, section and dimensions are all TechDraw's own, editable there. Inputs: bodies [names] (all when left out). views: from front, back, top, bottom, right, left, iso (front, top, right, iso when left out). projection: first | third (ISO first-angle or ASME third-angle). Left out, projection is TechDraw's preference, else third with inch units, else first; projectionFrom says which and why. paper: A4 | A3 | auto. scale: 0.5 is 1:2. Left out, scale is the largest standard scale (1:1, 2:1, 1:2 …) that fits. dimensions: false leaves the overall sizes off. hidden: true dashes hidden edges. name: the title of the sheet. file: a name in the folder of the session, or a path. The extension is dropped, and the three files share the stem. page: false writes the files only and adds nothing to the document. dims [{ view, kind: length (a, b, along h|v, offset mm) | diameter | radius (a: a round edge), fit "H7" or plus/minus mm, label }]. In dims, a and b are a point [x, y, z] or a query { body, kind, type, radius, near }. dims adds feature dimensions with tolerances or ISO 286 fits, with the limits written in. holes: true (every round hole called out where a view sees it end on) or the name of a view. holeFits { "6": "H7" }. titleBlock { title, partNumber, revision, material, finish, drawnBy, date, checkedBy, company, generalTolerance }. Ask the person for their titleBlock, and never make a name up. section: a straight view to draw as a full section. sectionAt: mm from the middle towards the viewer. sectionLabel: the letter (A). Traps: every call adds a NEW page, with its template, views and dimensions. When you redraw, object_delete the old page first. The PDF and SVG come from TechDraw only with FreeCAD's window up. Headless, they come from Workshop's sheet writer; filesFrom says which and why. TechDraw works out the lines of a view on another thread, so the call waits for them. It waits 30 s a view, and longer for a view of many edges (page.viewLimit, 240 s at most). The overall sizes go on each view when it is drawn, also when it is drawn late. coarse: true draws the views with the faster polygon lines of TechDraw. Left out, coarse is true for an assembly of over 3000 edges when holes is not asked. lines says which and why. A changing tool cannot run as a job. Vertex and edge numbers of a view change when the model does, so dimensions are made here, not carried over. Refused: a view that is not one of the seven. Refused: a section of iso or of a view not drawn. Refused: a scale of 0 or under. Refused: dims with a view not drawn, or a kind other than length, diameter, radius. Refused: holes naming a view not drawn. Refused: nothing fits the paper. The answer holds: files { svg, pdf, dxf paths }, filesFrom, paper, scale ("1:2"), projection, projectionFrom, fill, views [{ view, at, size, scale }], dimensions, section { view, label, plane, cutFaces, cutLineIn }, holes [{ view, diameter, count, label, from, features, calloutOff }], holeTable, calloutsOff, titleBlock, techdrawPage (its label). It holds page, the state of the TechDraw page: views, notOnPage [{ view, type, value, item, why }], viewsInExport and settled among others. Or it holds pageNote: why there is no page. It holds timing (in milliseconds), note and step. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check. Every key of page and timing, and the behaviour in full: guide_read { topic: "drawing", section: "drawing_make in full" }. That is the layout, the exports, the waits for TechDraw, and where hole callouts go.

bodies.description: Bodies to draw; all when left out.

projection.description: first (ISO) or third (ASME). Left out: TechDraw's preference (General ▸ projection angle), else third with inch units, else first.

scale.description: 0.5 for 1:2, 2 for 2:1; left out, the largest standard one that fits.

file.description: Where the files go: a name (in the session's folder), or a path — absolute (its folder made) or under the session's folder; an extension given is dropped, and the PDF, SVG and DXF share the stem.

dims.description: Feature dimensions: [{ view, kind: length (a, b, along h|v, offset mm) | diameter | radius (a round edge), fit "H7" or plus/minus mm, label }]; a and b a point [x,y,z] or a query { body, kind, type, radius, near } (a circle's centre, an edge's middle).

holes.description: true: every round hole called out in a view that sees it end on (front, right, top …), grouped by size: "4× ⌀3.4"; FreeCAD's own Holes as made ("2× ⌀6.6 THRU ⌴⌀11 ↧6.4", a thread's size); holes no drawn view sees end on in a hole table. Or a view's name: only that view's.

holeFits.description: A fit per hole diameter for the callouts: { "6": "H7" }.

titleBlock.description: { title, partNumber, revision, material, finish, drawnBy, date, checkedBy, company, generalTolerance (ISO 2768-m to start) } — filled into TechDraw's title block (and the files' own); ask the person for theirs.

coarse.description: TechDraw's coarse (polygon) lines for the views: faster on a large assembly. Left out: true over 3000 edges when holes is not asked.

drawing_exploded.description: Make an assembly manual. steps (required) [{ title, add: [bodies], note }], in the order the parts go together. A body goes in once; a second time is refused, naming its step. Each step is an isometric picture (SVG). In it, the parts already in place stay, and the new ones are moved off by explode mm. Left out, explode is 0.6 of the largest size, at least 10. direction up lifts the new parts over their places; out moves them away from the middle. A trail shows where each part goes, and a balloon gives its item number. It writes the steps and <name>_assembly.md with a bill of materials to the folder of the session. In the bill, bodies of the same shape are one item. Each item has the material and mass where part_spec or material_set recorded one. It has how each is made, from its setup, and Fasteners Workbench hardware by its own name. name: the stem of the files. title: the heading of the manual. Where every body is in one FreeCAD Assembly, this also CHANGES THE DOCUMENT. The moves become the Assembly's own Exploded View, editable there. The parts of step k move k − 1 explode lengths up, or out from step 2 on. Unless page: false, it also adds an ordinary TechDraw page of it. The page has a balloon per item and the bill of materials. Each call adds another Exploded View and page. Delete the old ones (object_delete) before you make it again. Outside an Assembly, route says that the steps use Workshop's own exploded shapes. Then, unless page: false, a blank TechDraw page shows the picture of the last step as a symbol. pageShows says which step. So the window shows the result. With page: false, nothing is added, and the call is still one (empty) undo step. So a history_undo straight after it takes back nothing in the document. Trap: each part is lifted over where it is in the document, so put the parts where they go first. warnings names parts that lie apart from the ones before them. The answer holds: manual (the .md path), steps [{ step, title, adds [{ item, part, qty }], svg }], bom [{ item, part, bodies, size, material, massG, madeBy }], explode, notInAnyStep, warnings, route. In an Assembly it holds routeNote | explodedView, assembly, moves, page | pageNote. Outside an Assembly it holds page, pageShows | pageNote. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

page.description: A TechDraw page of the Assembly's Exploded View (true by default; in an Assembly), else of the last step's picture.

patent_figures.description: Make patent-style figures FIG. 1 … of bodies (all when left out), one per view. views: from front, back, top, bottom, right, left, iso (iso, front, top, right when left out). The figures are black line art on A4 portrait within the USPTO's margins, with no hidden lines or shading. Each part gets its reference numeral (10, 20, 30 …), 3.5 mm high. A lead line goes to a face of the part that the viewer sees. Or give numerals { "body": n }, with the body named by its label or its object's name as bodies takes it. Each numeral is a whole number over 0, and each its own. The numerals of the answer go by label. A part hidden behind others in a view gets no numeral there (notSeenIn). It writes an SVG and a PDF per figure to the folder of the session. It also writes a list of the numerals there. name is the stem of the files and the label of the pages. Unless page: false, each figure is also added to the document as an ordinary TechDraw page in that style. The page has a blank template and visible lines only. The numerals are TechDraw balloons without a bubble, editable in TechDraw. This changes the document, one page a figure. Every call adds new pages, so object_delete the old ones first. The files are the page's own exports where TechDraw can write them (FreeCAD's window up). Else they come from Workshop's sheet writer (filesFrom says which and why). page: false writes the files only and changes nothing. After the export of each page, nothing of it stays marked as changed. TechDraw's export marks the template; the description of drawing_make says how this works. The row of a figure holds settled { cleared, waited, exportMs, turns, turnMs, seen, late, left } only in three cases. That is: a mark stayed (left), a mark can still come after the call (late), or nothing could be watched. The row of each figure always holds timing { sheet, page, export { wait, scene, svg, check, pdf }, settle, turns, turnMs, total }, in milliseconds, as drawing_make's. sheet: Workshop's own projection and labels. page: the TechDraw page, with the lines of its view waited for. export: TechDraw's SVG and PDF and what they need first. settle: the wait after the export. turns and turnMs: the turns of FreeCAD's event loop run for the figure, and the time inside them. The answer also holds timing { figures, turns, turnMs, total } for the whole call. Refused: a view that is not one of these. Refused: a numeral that is not a whole number over 0. Refused: a numeral used twice, or for a body not drawn. It takes seconds per figure (exact hidden-line removal), longer for a detailed assembly. The answer holds: figures [{ fig, view, page | pageNote, svg, pdf, filesFrom, settled, timing }], numerals { label: n }, list (the numerals file), notSeenIn, timing, note. patent_draft uses the numerals and figures of the last call in this session. The answer of a changing call can also hold health { ok, verdict, todo } from the shared check.

patent_draft.description: Write a Markdown draft of a patent description and a claims skeleton to the folder of the session. title (required): what the invention is, in a few words. field and background: your words, used as given. bodies: left out, those of the last patent_figures, else all. name: the stem of the file. It describes the bodies from the model: their sizes, and which adjoin which. It uses the numerals and figures of the last patent_figures in this session. Run that first; without it, the draft has no figures or numerals. It leaves in brackets what only the inventor and counsel can say. It is a starting point for the review of a patent attorney, and the file says so. Never present it as ready to file. It is never filed or sent anywhere. Changes nothing in the document. The answer holds: draft (the path), numerals, figures (how many), adjoining [[a, b] …], note.

library_pack.description: Pack bodies to share as one zip in the folder of the session. The zip holds each body as STEP and STL, and a README with their sizes, material and mass. The README also holds the print settings from their print setup (magnet pauses too). The zip also holds a LICENSE and credits. formats: ["step", "stl"]; both when left out. tolerance: mm, for the STL. license (required): CC-BY-4.0, CC-BY-SA-4.0, CC0-1.0 or MIT. Ask the person: the license decides what others may do with the parts. author is required for all but CC0: the name they want shown; a handle will do. credits [{ title, author, url, license, changes }] for remixed parts. credits is refused when the licence of a credited part does not allow the one chosen (no-derivatives, non-commercial, share-alike). bodies [names] (all when left out). name: the title of the pack. description: the opening of the README. The STEP header holds the name of the file and the author given: no path, user name or organisation. personal names any file that still has one. provider auto (default): ScanRuler-FreeCAD's pack when that add-on is installed (through Agent Link's library_pack service), else Documents' own. provider documents forces Documents' own. by says which made it. serviceNote says when the service failed and Documents' own made it instead. Refused: no licence, or one not listed. Refused: no author where the licence needs one. Refused: credits that are not a list of objects. Refused: formats other than step and stl. Refused: no body in the document. Meshing a detailed body for the STL takes a while. Changes nothing in the document. The answer holds: pack (the zip's path), files, license, parts [{ files, size }], bytes, by, warnings, unsound { bodies, note }, personal { files, note }. unsound: body_check says the bodies are not sound; fix them before sharing.

provider.description: auto (ScanRuler's pack when installed, else Documents') or documents.
